# Context & Memory Principles {.unnumbered}

Part II develops the AI-native three-tier memory hierarchy. Context capacity is the L1 cache of neural compute: expressive, fast, strictly bounded, and quadratically expensive in compute and linearly in memory. Runtimes must actively manage context working sets, exploit Radix prefix caching and PCIe paging in L2, and safeguard L3 episodic storage against state poisoning.

::: {#pri-vol3-attention-working-set .callout-principle title="The Attention Working Set"}

**Invariant**: Context capacity is an active L1 working-set cache governed by physical accelerator memory bandwidth and HBM capacity limits.

**Implication**: Treating large context windows as infinite garbage bins triggers Time-To-First-Token explosion and lost-in-the-middle attention degradation.

:::

::: {#pri-vol3-prefix-locality .callout-principle title="Prefix Locality and Coherence"}

**Invariant**: Multi-turn agent loops exhibit massive prompt prefix sharing; runtimes must exploit Radix-tree KV reuse and page idle KV blocks during tool stalls.

**Implication**: Mutating dynamic tokens at prompt beginnings invalidates entire prefix trees; prompt layouts must be strictly engineered with static prefixes first.

:::

::: {#pri-vol3-episodic-consolidation .callout-principle title="Hierarchical Memory Consolidation"}

**Invariant**: Multi-session agent longevity requires episodic storage governed by vector retrieval, structured graphs, and temporal decay, guarded against persistent state poisoning.

**Implication**: Address translation in episodic memory is lossy and non-deterministic; persistent stores must be sanitized against sleeper prompt injection attacks.

:::
